content.user_title: Transform JSON Data with Query and Schema Tools
content.value_statement: JSON changes often need careful reshaping, validation, and format conversion. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical patterns for reliable JSON work.
actual_capabilities: Parse and pretty-print JSON from strings or local files.
Validate documents against JSON Schema examples.
Extract fields with JSONPath, JMESPath, and jq patterns.
Flatten, unflatten, merge, filter, sort, and deduplicate JSON structures.
Convert JSON to CSV, YAML, and XML using documented examples.
Generate basic JSON Schema from sample data.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a packaged executable transformer.
Large files may need streaming parsers beyond the included examples.
External libraries such as jsonschema, jmespath, DeepDiff, or jq must be installed separately.
The skill does not verify data privacy or business rules automatically.

use_cases.title: Clean API Responses
use_cases.description: Map nested API payloads into smaller application records with validation.

use_cases.title: Prepare Data Exports
use_cases.description: Convert JSON collections into CSV, YAML, or XML for reporting workflows.

use_cases.title: Review Schema Changes
use_cases.description: Compare JSON versions, inspect field changes, and draft validation schemas.

prompt_templates.title: Format and Validate JSON
prompt_templates.prompt: Use json-transformer on [file]. Validate the JSON, list any errors, and provide a readable formatted result.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Target Fields
prompt_templates.prompt: Use json-transformer to extract [fields] from [file]. Show the matching paths and explain any missing values.

prompt_templates.title: Flatten for Spreadsheet Import
prompt_templates.prompt: Use json-transformer to flatten [file] for spreadsheet import. Preserve original field meaning and note arrays that need review.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Versions and Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use json-transformer to compare [old file] and [new file]. Summarize schema changes, data type changes, and migration risks.

output_examples.input: A malformed configuration export from a staging service.
A nested customer export that must become a spreadsheet.
Two API response versions from separate releases.

best_practices: Validate source JSON before transforming it.
Keep a copy of original files before writing output files.
Document path queries and merge rules for repeatable results.
anti_patterns: Do not overwrite source files before checking transformed output.
Do not assume arrays are uniform without sampling edge cases.
Do not merge untrusted configuration without validation rules.

faq.question: Does this skill run transformations by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and examples for an AI assistant to apply with user approval.

faq.question: Can it validate JSON Schema?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Python and JavaScript examples for validating data against JSON Schema.

faq.question: Can it convert JSON to CSV?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents CSV conversion patterns and jq commands for tabular exports.

faq.question: Does it support JSONPath and JMESPath?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for both query styles and explains common extraction patterns.

faq.question: Is it suitable for very large files?
faq.answer: It can guide the approach, but very large files may require streaming parsers.

faq.question: Does it protect sensitive data automatically?
faq.answer: No. Users should review inputs and outputs for secrets before sharing transformed data.
